indicator.title: Eingehende Rücküberweisungen
indicator.description: Rücküberweisungen, die in die berichtende Volkswirtschaft eingehen, in Millionen laufenden US-Dollar.

workbookNotes: Note: All numbers are in current (nominal) US $

For a discussion of the definition of remittances, see "Workers' Remittances: An Important and Stable Source of External Development Finance", Global Development Finance 2003, World Bank. Data since 2005 are based on IMF BOP Statistics that use the definitions of IMF BPM6.
For additional information, please also see "International Transactions in Remittances: Guide for Compilers and Users", International Monetary Fund, 2009.

* In the past, remittance figures for China were adding some portions of other current transfers as a third component to the sum of personal transfers and compensation of employees to adjust for discrepancies in official reporting, underreported informal transfers, and potentially misclassification of

remittance statistics. As of 2025, however, China’s remittance data are only including components of personal transfers and compensation of employees that are reported in IMF’s Balance of Payment to be in conformity with guidelines outlines in the IMF’s Remittances Guide for Compilers and
the World Bank’s World Development Indicator. For example, inward remittance flows to China will be $31.4 billion in 2024 compared to $47.4 billion of previous concept.
